account: It is noon on day 0, and I am home for my scheduled lunch after attending the ten o'clock market walk. The main unusual thing I have heard is repeated news that the baker was carrying a sack of bread at the inn. Several townsfolk repeated it, but I did not see it myself. A sack means a substantial bread load, though I do not know the amount or purpose. It could simply be a delivery to the inn; I have no evidence of wrongdoing or a shortage. The builder has been seeking the innkeeper or freight operator about supplies, but I have not learned which supplies or whether there is a problem. These matters might be ordinary trade, and I cannot yet connect them. My secretary has been helping confirm appointment directions. The neighbour expects me for tea at three at the east-bank cottage beside the ferry, road point (16,-60,105). I have two fresh loaves purchased at the market, intended for lunch and tea. Next I am due at the office at thirteen hundred for town accounts, then tea, the office at sixteen thirty, and home at nineteen hundred.
